label: CRS210-8G-2S+IN
description: MikroTik CRS210-8G-2S+IN (CRS210-8G-2S+IN) — 8x 1G RJ45, 2x 10G SFP+. Powered by the DC jack or by passive/802.3af/at PoE-in on eth1 only (10-57 V). 1-core QCA8519.
notes: Vendor rows read 2026-11-28 from https://mikrotik.com/product/CRS210-8G-2SplusIN: **Number of DC inputs 2 (DC jack, PoE-IN)**, **PoE in Passive PoE**, **PoE in input Voltage 10-57 V**, **802.3af support Yes**, **Max power consumption 13 W** and **Max power consumption without attachments 13W**. The datasheet names the socket: "Power options: 10-57V, 24V 0.8A PSU included, PoE in: 10-57V on Ether1 (802.3af/at or passive PoE)" (https://cdn.mikrotik.com/web-assets/product_files/CRS210-8G-2SplusIN-141211150201_141201.pdf). So eth1 is the inlet and draws the board ceiling of 13 W - 0.05 W above 802.3af class 3's 12.95 W PD allowance, which is why the sheet also prints 802.3at, and why the passive 10-57 V injector it ships with is the honest way to power it. eth2-eth8 declare poeIn: false: the CRS210 sources no PoE at all, so nothing beside the inlet can be fed. The seven silent sockets had been inheriting the 12.95 W guess from the poe-pd capability, 90.65 W from a 13 W switch. Also from the same datasheet: SFP+1 takes 1.25G and 10G modules, SFP+2 takes 10G modules only.
